title: opt-A productionized: ChunkedGraphTrainer (per-chunk CUDA graphs, weights bitwise over multi-step training)
config: d12 bf16, b=1, chunk=16384, production env (HEAD_FP8=2, IDX_MODE=hsi-auto, CKPT=state CKPT_EVERY=2, fused ATTN_V2/MHC_V3/MOE_*/RMS/SWIGLU/WOA/ROPE)

design.captured: per-chunk loss (length-weighted) + backward, plus tiny writes that publish per-chunk and total loss into static device buffers
design.outside_graphs: optimizer.step(), detach_leaked_buffers, loss readout, cache zeroing, data copy into static input buffers
design.static_inputs: caller-owned buffers dict (e.g. ids [1,total]); step(ids=...) does buf.copy_(ids) before replay
design.memory: one shared torch.cuda.graph_pool_handle() across all chunk graphs, replayed in order
design.guards: p.grad storage identity checked every step (forbids zero_grad(set_to_none=True)); capture failure recorded in .capture_error and step() falls back to eager; capture=False = eager mode (CPU/debug)
design.capture_recipe: 1 main-stream eager pass (grad alloc), 2 side-stream warmup passes, then one graph per chunk; capture is one-time (~12 s at 262K, ~50 s at 1M)
design.capture_safe_loss: FP8 CE head (HEAD_FP8=2) + grouped Triton MoE; the reference MoE loop (bincount().tolist()) and the bf16 CE head backward sync with the host and cannot be captured (documented in the module)

integration_g5_bench_graph.context: chunked CUDA graphs: fwd+loss+bwd per chunk captured, optimizer/logging outside; weights updated in place

host_variance_note: same-process A/B is authoritative. The graph step is GPU-bound and stable across hosts (1M: 10.72 s here vs 10.92 s on the bj-B1 host); the eager step is CPU-launch-bound and host-dependent (1M: 12.17 s here vs 13.72 s on bj-B1, both after the §3v attention fix). Hence the graph delta is -11.9% on this (faster-CPU) host and -20.4% on bj-B1, but the absolute graph step time is within 2%.
tests: tests/test_chunk_graph.py: CPU eager==manual bitwise; CUDA replay grads + 2-step training weights/losses bitwise vs eager (passed on the 5090, 12.7 s).
